neighbours.label: The preposition inside a fixed stake/petition verb idiom: 'on' in 'put X on the line' and 'for' in 'file for divorce/bankruptcy', not literal prepositions
fire: Firefighters put their own lives on the line every time they enter a burning house.
The senator put her whole career on the line by voting against the bill.
After the factory closed, the owners had no choice but to file for bankruptcy.
Months after the wedding, the singer quietly decided to file for divorce.
Thousands of laid-off workers rushed to file for unemployment benefits in April.
He is willing to put his reputation on the line to defend the project.
Journalists who report from war zones put their safety on the line daily.
The struggling airline was forced to file for protection from its creditors.
quiet: She hung the wet towels on the line in the backyard to dry.
When the lights came up, the senator set her coffee cup on the desk.
Once the factory closed, the owners sold the building to a developer.
A few months after the wedding, the singer moved to a farm in Ohio.
Thousands of workers waited for the bus outside the plant in April.
He stacked his books on the shelf to clear space on the table.
Reporters in war zones often sleep on the floor of crowded hotels.
The clerk asked him to file the forms in the cabinet by the door.
